# signet-protocol (Rust)

> Native Rust apps that verify Signet identity events on Nostr have to
> reimplement the NIP-01 canonical event id and the kind-21236 auth event
> shape from scratch, and drift from the TypeScript reference. signet-protocol
> is the Rust counterpart of the `signet-protocol` npm package: same wire
> format, cross-impl test vectors, one source of truth.

For engine and appliance authors who need Signet verification outside
JavaScript: voxel games, embedded signing hardware, custom Nostr relays,
native multiplayer servers. The canonical event id computed here matches the
TypeScript `signet-protocol` package; signature verification is planned.

## Getting Started

Not yet published to crates.io; depend on the repository, pinned to a commit:

```toml
[dependencies]
signet-protocol = { git = "https://github.com/forgesworn/signet-protocol-rs", rev = "4f42cc86c80674d575802ddb77d179b5318c9329" }
```

Minimum supported Rust version: 1.74 (the `rust-version` declared in
`Cargo.toml`).

```rust
use signet_protocol::{canonical_id, AUTH_EVENT_KIND};

let pubkey = [0xbbu8; 32];
let tags = vec![
    vec!["challenge".to_string(), "a".repeat(64)],
    vec!["origin".to_string(), "https://localhost:8094".to_string()],
];
let id = canonical_id(&pubkey, 1_700_000_000, AUTH_EVENT_KIND, &tags, "");
// `id` is a raw [u8; 32]. hex::encode(id) (hex crate, not re-exported by this
// crate) gives the lower-case hex string to compare with the event's `.id`.
```

## Key Concepts

- **Canonical event id**: the NIP-01 serialisation (compact JSON, lower-case
  hex pubkey) hashed with SHA-256; the basis every verifier compares against
  an event's `.id` field.
- **Auth events (kind 21236)**: `Sign in with Signet` events, carrying a
  `challenge` and `origin` tag pair that a server must check.
- **Credentials (kind 31000)**: verifiable attestations (display-name,
  age-scope, professional) sharing one kind, differentiated by a `type` tag.
- **Cross-impl vectors**: the same test vectors run against the TypeScript
  package, so the two implementations cannot silently diverge.

## API Surface

- `canonical_id(pubkey: &[u8; 32], created_at: u32, kind: u32, tags: &[Vec<String>], content: &str) -> [u8; 32]`:
  the NIP-01 canonical event id. `pubkey` is the raw 32-byte x-only key, not
  hex. Hex-encode the result (for example `hex::encode(id)`) to compare with
  a Nostr event's `.id` string.
- `AUTH_EVENT_KIND`: `u32` constant, `21236`.
- `CREDENTIAL_KIND`: `u32` constant, `31000`.
- `SignetAuthEvent`: typed kind-21236 event struct. Fields: `pubkey: [u8; 32]`
  (x-only Schnorr key), `created_at: u32` (Unix seconds), `kind: u32` (must
  equal `AUTH_EVENT_KIND`), `tags: Vec<Vec<String>>` (must include
  `["challenge", <hex>]` and `["origin", <str>]`), `content: String` (must be
  empty for auth events), `id: [u8; 32]` (SHA-256 of the canonical
  serialisation; recompute with `canonical_id`), `sig: [u8; 64]` (BIP-340
  Schnorr signature over `id`; not verified by this crate), `from_np: bool`.
- `from_np`: a client-asserted flag that the event was signed by a Natural
  Person keypair; a server that rejects Natural Persons as players should
  reject `true`.
- `SignetCredential`: typed kind-31000 credential struct. Same fields and
  types as `SignetAuthEvent` except there is no `from_np`.

Structs are data only in 0.1: build them with struct literals. They derive
`Clone` and `Debug` only; there is no constructor, parser or serde support
yet, so deserialising JSON into them with `serde_json` will not compile.

Schnorr verification, full auth-event verification, credential verification
and the server-side challenge nonce table are planned; not yet shipped.

- [README](./README.md): install, status, and the case for a separate Rust
  crate.
- [Signet protocol](https://github.com/forgesworn/signet): the protocol this
  crate implements.
